config.title: Star Rating Component

intro.title: Star Rating Component
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Star Rating component that allows users to select a rating from 1 to 5 stars. You will learn how to use Vue's reactive state to track the current rating and the rating being hovered over. The component will involve using v-for to render stars dynamically and event handlers like @click and @mouseover to update the display. By the end, you'll have a functional, interactive rating widget that visually responds to user input.
intro.usecase: Star rating components are ubiquitous in modern web applications where user feedback and content quality indicators are essential. You'll find them in e-commerce platforms like Amazon for product reviews, streaming services like Netflix for content ratings, and booking sites like Airbnb for property evaluations. As a Vue developer, you'll implement these interactive elements in product dashboards, review forms, and content management systems where users visually rate items. Mastering this component teaches you how to create reusable, accessible UI controls that capture user input while providing immediate visual feedback.

objectives: Construct a Vue component with reactive state to manage a dynamic star rating value.
Implement a method to update the rating based on user interaction with click events.
Render a visual star rating display using conditional class binding for filled and empty stars.
Configure the component to accept and utilize a maximum rating limit as a prop.
Integrate the star rating component into a parent view and display the current rating value.
Manipulate the component's appearance by applying CSS classes based on the rating state.

steps.title: Import Vue and ref from vue
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and ref from the vue module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing from a package
import { createApp } from 'vue'
steps.seedCode: // Import Vue and ref from 'vue' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue framework and ref reactivity function are available for use in the component.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package to proceed.

steps.title: Create the StarRating component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named StarRating using the setup function. The component should return an empty template for now.
steps.hint: Define a component with the name StarRating and use the setup function to return an empty template.
steps.seedCode:
import { ref } from 'vue'

// Create the StarRating component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A StarRating component is defined with a setup function that returns an empty template.
successCriteria: The StarRating component is created with a setup function that returns a template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the component, but make sure it's named StarRating and uses the setup function to return a template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Ensure you define a component named StarRating with a setup function that returns a template.

steps.title: Initialize rating state with ref
steps.instruction: Inside your StarRating component, declare a reactive state variable called 'rating' using ref, initialized to 0.
steps.hint: Use the ref function you imported earlier to create a reactive reference with an initial value of 0.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: reactive state with ref
const count = ref(0)
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a reactive rating state variable that starts at 0.
successCriteria: A 'rating' variable is declared using ref(0) inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref(0) to initialize the rating variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The rating state wasn't properly initialized. Use ref(0) to create a reactive reference.

steps.title: Define the setRating handler
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named setRating that takes a newRating parameter and updates the rating ref's value to newRating.
steps.hint: Create a function that accepts a parameter and assigns it to rating.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a setRating handler function that can update the rating state when called.
successCriteria: A setRating function is defined inside setup that updates rating.value with its parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure setRating takes a parameter and assigns it to rating.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The setRating handler isn't defined correctly. It should be a function that updates rating.value.

steps.title: Return rating and setRating from setup
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, return an object containing the rating reactive variable and setRating handler so they can be used in the template.
steps.hint: The return statement in setup should expose the reactive state and methods you want to use in your template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The setup function now returns an object with rating and setRating, making them available for use in the component template.
successCriteria: The setup function returns an object containing both rating and setRating.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning both rating and setRating from the setup function. Check that your return statement includes both variables.
steps.feedbackWrong: The setup function needs to return an object containing both rating and setRating. Without this, the template won't have access to these values.

steps.title: Add the main container div
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function's return statement, add a div element as the component's template root.
steps.hint: The return statement should now include a div element. This will serve as the container for your star rating UI.
steps.expectedOutcome: The setup function now returns a div element, establishing the component's root template structure.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a div element as the root template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a div element inside the return statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement should contain a div element as the root template. Check that you've added it correctly.

steps.title: Add a heading for the component
steps.instruction: Inside the main container div, add an h2 heading with the text 'Star Rating Component'.
steps.hint: Add an <h2> element with the heading text inside the div that was created in the previous step.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a heading element

My Component Title
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a visible heading that identifies it as a star rating component.
successCriteria: An h2 element with the text 'Star Rating Component' is added inside the main container div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a heading, but check if it's an h2 element with the exact text 'Star Rating Component'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The heading wasn't added correctly. Make sure to add an h2 element with 'Star Rating Component' inside the main div.

steps.title: Create a stars container div
steps.instruction: In the setup function's return object, add a div element with the class 'stars-container' after the heading element.
steps.hint: Remember to place the div after the existing heading. Use the template syntax to return the div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component's template now includes a div element with class 'stars-container' that will hold the star elements.
successCriteria: The return object contains a div property with class 'stars-container' placed after the h2 property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a div element with the correct class name 'stars-container' in the return object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The stars container div is missing or incorrect. Check that you've added it to the return object with the proper class.

steps.title: Render star buttons with v-for
steps.instruction: Inside the stars container div, use v-for to create 5 button elements. Each button should have a key attribute set to its index.
steps.hint: Use v-for="(star, index) in 5" to iterate 5 times and create buttons. Remember to add :key="index" to each button.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: rendering multiple items with v-for
steps.expectedOutcome: The stars container now contains 5 button elements generated by v-for, each with a unique key.
successCriteria: The stars container has 5 button elements created using v-for, each with a :key attribute.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have exactly 5 buttons and each has a :key attribute.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using v-for inside the stars container to create 5 button elements with keys.

steps.title: Add star icons and dynamic classes
steps.instruction: Inside the v-for loop, add a star icon (★) to each button and bind a dynamic class that applies 'active' when the star index is less than or equal to the current rating.
steps.hint: Use the button's text content for the star icon. For the class binding, use :class with an object that checks if index < rating.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: dynamic class binding
<button :class="{ active: index < rating }">★</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: Each star button will display a star icon and have visual feedback (active styling) based on the current rating.
successCriteria: Star buttons display ★ icons and have dynamic class binding that applies 'active' class conditionally based on rating.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the star icon, but the dynamic class binding might be missing or incorrect. Check the condition for applying the 'active' class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The star icons or dynamic class binding are not implemented as required. Review the v-for loop structure and :class binding syntax.

steps.title: Wire click events to setRating
steps.instruction: Add a click event listener to each star button that calls the setRating function with the appropriate star index.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive on the button element inside your v-for loop. Pass the current star index (i+1) as an argument to setRating.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring a click event in Vue
<button @click="handleClick(index)">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: Each star button will respond to clicks by updating the rating state.
successCriteria: All star buttons have @click event listeners that call setRating with the appropriate star value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure each star button has an @click attribute that calls setRating with the correct star number.
steps.feedbackWrong: The click events aren't properly wired. Check that you've added @click to each button and passed the correct argument to setRating.

element that shows rating.value using template interpolation.
